name: Dina Valenzuela

physical_description.hair_color: Black with premature silvering at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Closely cropped, faded sides, kept severe and functional
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-deep brown with golden and olive undertones from the blending of Hispanic/Latin American and Southeast Asian ancestry—rich and complex rather than uniform, with slight variation across the face and a subtle luminosity that catches light across the cheekbones and bridge of nose
physical_description.complexion: Weathered face with deep lines around the eyes—squint-marks from years of calculating blast radiuses and reading building blueprints. Strong, angular cheekbones characteristic of both Southeast Asian and Latin American heritage, creating high, defined facial planes. A three-inch scar runs from his left cheekbone to jaw, white and precise, creating contrast against his skin. Sparse, deliberate facial hair—five-day stubble maintained as a styling choice, not neglect. Hands are calloused, fingers slightly stiff from old shrapnel injuries. Subtle epicanthic fold variation visible at the outer corners of his eyes from Southeast Asian heritage, integrated naturally within broader eye structure.
distinguishing_marks: Scar from left cheekbone to jaw—thin, surgical-looking, likely from a controlled demolition gone wrong in his thirties
Burn scar across the back of his right shoulder, mottled and old, visible only when his shirt is removed
Faded tattooed grid pattern on his left forearm—structural calculations or a memorial to a job; never explains it
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Subdermal reinforcement plating visible as faint geometric ridges under the skin of both wrists and knuckles—silverish, barely perceptible unless you know what you're looking at. His left eye has a barely-noticeable neural port behind the ear, marked by a small dermal seal. No flashy chrome; everything chosen for discrete functionality.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with feet shoulder-width apart, a habit from standing near detonation zones. Moves with deliberate economy—no wasted motion. When thinking, he touches his jaw scar absently. Speaks quietly, forcing others to lean in. His hands are steady, even when discussing volatile materials.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 utilitarian: heavy-duty Carhartt-equivalent work pants in tan or charcoal, always with multiple reinforced pockets for tools and detonator components. Layered shirts—functional base layer, usually a fitted black tee under an unbuttoned work shirt or lightweight tactical jacket in muted colors (grays, earth tones). Steel-toed boots, worn but meticulously maintained. A weathered leather jacket, vintage pre-2200 quality, hangs in his Geartown workshop. No logos, no status symbols. Everything is built for durability and function. Wears a simple steel wedding band on his left hand—never removes it.
